references.hachimiBehavior: Workbench projects Session/Run/TranscriptItem as Codex-style thread/turn/item lifecycle with typed plan, Diff, command, collaboration, and user-input state.
references.acceptance: Typed lifecycle replay, semantic timeline rendering, run summaries, blocking input gates, cross-session activity, and Codex-style layout tests pass.

references.hachimiBehavior: A project Session may bind to the original local checkout and expose live baseline Diff, branch, commit, safe push, activity, and source state. Cloud execution and PR/MR status are not implemented.
references.acceptance: Environment snapshot, Git mutation fencing, safe push, source capture, activity selection, and pinned-summary tests pass.

references.hachimiBehavior: Each project Session reuses one managed worktree and may transactionally hand off staged, unstaged, untracked, and explicitly included ignored files between Local and managed Worktree checkouts.
references.acceptance: Round-trip, managed-worktree reuse, target drift fencing, snapshot reconstruction, rollback, and startup reconciliation tests pass.

references.hachimiBehavior: The Windows built-in browser uses a persistent, app-isolated CEF profile and exposes the same visible tab to the user and the Run-owned Agent lease. Automatic upload is not exposed; TLS verification remains enabled.
references.acceptance: Workspace/tab persistence, CEF child-window rendering, error-page mapping, observation fencing, standard actions, Runtime integrity, and Chrome-extension isolation are the current implemented gates. Persistent per-site Agent grants, downloads, and full-CDP approval remain incomplete until their dedicated gates pass.

references.hachimiBehavior: A paired extension may act only in task-owned Chrome tabs under exact site and capability decisions.
references.acceptance: Pairing, task tab ownership, site policy, DNR, takeover, history, and CDP tests pass.

references.hachimiBehavior: Computer observe/act is app-scoped, user-takeover aware, integrity fenced, and screenshot bytes remain memory-only.
references.acceptance: Frame lifecycle, app/window fencing, takeover, integrity boundaries, limits, error cleanup, and no-temp-file tests pass.

references.hachimiBehavior: Plugin contributions are content-addressed and cannot bypass Host, sandbox, approval, connector, or MCP authority.
references.acceptance: Manifest, permission-diff, revision drift, runtime binding, connector/MCP authority, and reconciliation tests pass.

references.hachimiBehavior: Standalone, Session-continuation, timer, and typed Event schedules use one TaskRun ledger and explicit persistent authority.
references.acceptance: Timing, Event ingress, grants, overlap, retry, NeedsAttention, stop, worktree, and restart reconciliation tests pass.

references.hachimiBehavior: Responses uses strict public Item and SSE shapes; only public summaries are displayable and opaque compaction state is not interpreted.
references.acceptance: Responses JSON/SSE, function calls, usage, cancellation, errors, summaries, compaction fallback, and capability drift pass conformance.

references.hachimiBehavior: Chat Completions remains an explicit provider protocol and never claims Responses-only capabilities.
references.acceptance: JSON/SSE, text, function calls, usage, finish reason, cancellation, errors, overflow, and malformed response tests pass.

references.hachimiBehavior: Embeddings are exposed through a provider-neutral interface without creating or populating Memory.
references.acceptance: Input ordering, index, finite vector, dimensions, usage, cancellation, HTTP error, and malformed response tests pass.
